Add custom action button to widget header (#79)

Introduces a configurable action button in the floating widget header that allows
host apps to trigger custom actions. Includes native module support for iOS and
Android, with event callbacks and full UI integration. The WidgetBridge communication
layer has been refactored to use NotificationCenter for cleaner cross-runtime messaging.

Co-authored-by: Claude Haiku 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add dynamic WebSocket server URL switching (#77)

* Add dynamic WebSocket server URL switching to expo-air widget

Implement setServerUrl() native function on iOS and Android to allow changing the widget's WS server URL and secret at runtime. The widget automatically disconnects from the old server and reconnects to the new one via the existing useEffect dependency in useWebSocketMessages.

Add example app UI with server URL and secret inputs to test the feature end-to-end.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Fix Android updateServerUrl wiping all surface props

updateSurfaceProps does a full replacement (not merge), so passing only
serverUrl would drop size, color and expanded. Track current prop values
and rebuild the complete Bundle on every update, matching the iOS pattern.

fix: pass EXPO_PACKAGER_PROXY_URL to Metro via tunnel URL

fix: inject tunnel URL into dev launcher recently opened apps registry

RCTBundleURLProvider approach doesn't work because packagerServerHost
strips the port from jsLocation, then the compiled-in RCT_METRO_PORT
(8087) gets appended, creating a malformed tunnel URL.

Instead, register the tunnel URL directly in the dev launcher's
recently opened apps registry (UserDefaults). The dev launcher checks
this registry on startup and auto-connects to the most recent URL.
This bypasses RCTBundleURLProvider entirely.

feat: Add WebSocket authentication via auto-generated secret (#34)

* feat: Add WebSocket authentication via auto-generated secret

Add cryptographic secret-based authentication to the prompt server to prevent unauthorized access when exposed via tunnels. The secret is generated at startup, embedded as a query parameter in the server URL, and validated on every connection attempt.

Key changes:
- PromptServer constructor accepts optional secret parameter
- WebSocket connections and HTTP requests validated against secret
- Secret generated in DevEnvironment.startPromptServer() and propagated through all flows
- Secret embedded in server URLs: wss://tunnel?secret=<hex> or ws://localhost:port?secret=<hex>
- Secret masked in all console logs to prevent leakage
- HMR reconnect URL construction fixed to properly handle query parameters
- All entry points verified: fly, start, server, dev commands

This mitigates the critical vulnerability of unauthenticated access to a prompt server running Claude with bypassPermissions mode.
